name: Western

influenced_by: Hollywood Western films' romanticized visual mythology

media.title: Hollywood Western films of the 1930s-60s (John Ford's work especially)
media.note: the main vehicle that turned working ranch dress into a widely recognized fashion silhouette

reacts_against: nothing consistent across its many revivals; each wave (1950s, 1980s, 2020s) has drawn on the same source wardrobe for different reasons, from pure Hollywood romance to 2020s "yeehaw" irony.
article: Western fashion draws on real 19th-century American cattle-ranching workwear — denim built to withstand hard labor, leather chaps, sturdy boots — but the specific romanticized silhouette most people picture (fringe, turquoise jewelry, an idealized rugged individualism) owes at least as much to Hollywood Western films of the 1930s-60s, particularly John Ford's work, as to any actual period ranch photography. The look has resurfaced in fashion repeatedly and for different reasons each time: a 1980s "urban cowboy" trend tied to the film of the same name, a 2018-20 internet-driven "yeehaw agenda" that reclaimed Western style partly through Black country and hip-hop culture's own relationship to cowboy imagery, and a 2023-24 wave that arrived alongside — and partly overlapped with — the mob wife trend's maximalist mood. That repeated, differently-motivated cycling is typical of workwear-derived aesthetics on this list, where the garments' practical origin stays constant while their cultural meaning shifts with each revival.

findings: dark — about 45% of the measured color across 6 wiki images is below mid-lightness
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
